task_text: Reciprocal sliding transfer: Each arm holds a level scoop, a shallow square tray that is open on the side facing the other arm. A cube on a very slippery surface starts on the left scoop. Without tilting the scoops, the left arm must make the cube slide out over its open edge onto the right scoop, which must be moving in step with the left scoop (at 0.2 m/s or more) when the cube arrives and then brake to rest with the cube on it within 1.5 s. The right arm then carries it to a new place and makes it slide back the same way onto the left scoop, which must likewise be moving in step when it arrives and then brake to rest. Finally the cube must be set down on a fixed output platform and left there at rest. Until that final deposit begins, the scoops may not tilt by more than 2.1 deg, and the cube may never be without scoop contact for more than about a tenth of a second. Phases, in order: left_inertial_slip: while the cube is on the left scoop (it has touched that tool link within the last 25 ms), its centre has moved more than 0.028 m toward the open edge from its start offset, measured along the left scoop's tool x axis (left-tool-frame x > 0.040 + 0.028 = 0.068 m).; right_receive_and_brake: the cube is on the right scoop (touched within the last 25 ms) and not on the left one (no left-scoop contact within the last 25 ms), for 0.3 s without interruption. During that time its centre is within 0.065 m of the right scoop's floor centre along both tool x and tool y (|x|, |y| < 0.065 m in the right tool frame), and it moves at less than 0.05 m/s relative to the right scoop (the scoop's rigid-body velocity at the cube's position). The receive must be a matched, braked catch: when the cube last came onto the right scoop (the step at which it became supported by that scoop, i.e. touched it within the last 25 ms, after a step at which it was not), the right scoop's horizontal speed was at least `receiver_min_speed` = 0.20 m/s and its horizontal velocity differed from the left scoop's by at most `match_tolerance` = 0.05 m/s; throughout the 0.3 s the right scoop moves slower than `rest_speed` = 0.02 m/s (it has braked to rest); and the 0.3 s begin within `brake_window` = 1.5 s of that arrival. The right tool frame's position at the moment this phase completes is recorded as the receive pose.; reverse_geometry: with the cube on the right scoop (touched within the last 25 ms), the right tool frame is more than 0.06 m away from the receive pose recorded at the end of right_receive_and_brake.; left_receive_and_brake: the cube is on the left scoop (touched within the last 25 ms) and not on the right one (no right-scoop contact within the last 25 ms), for 0.3 s without interruption. During that time its centre is within 0.065 m of the left floor centre along both tool x and tool y, and it moves at less than 0.05 m/s relative to the left scoop. The receive must be a matched, braked catch: when the cube last came onto the left scoop (the step at which it became supported by that scoop, i.e. touched it within the last 25 ms, after a step at which it was not), the left scoop's horizontal speed was at least `receiver_min_speed` = 0.20 m/s and its horizontal velocity differed from the right scoop's by at most `match_tolerance` = 0.05 m/s; throughout the 0.3 s the left scoop moves slower than `rest_speed` = 0.02 m/s (it has braked to rest); and the 0.3 s begin within `brake_window` = 1.5 s of that arrival.; final_support_deposit: the cube touches the output platform and has touched neither scoop within the last 25 ms, for 0.5 s without interruption. During that time its centre is within 0.065 m horizontally (a circle) of the platform's centre (the platform top is 0.20 x 0.15 m), and it moves slower than 0.04 m/s. This completes the task.
